author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory, reached at GET /specialties.html, lists every specialty by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, shown by full name, all on one page. It has no navigation entry and no inbound link.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it
given a veterinarian listed under a specialty, then they are shown by first name followed by last name (for example "Helen Leary")
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the page is opened, then they are listed under each one
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear
given any number of specialties, when the page is opened, then all of them are shown on one page with no pagination
given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the page is opened, then it is still listed and shown as held by none rather than left blank
given the page is opened twice, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same stable order
given a clinic with no specialties, when the page is opened, then it renders with an empty listing rather than failing
given the page's own wording, then it is present in every supported language, while specialty names show as stored
given the other pages of the system, when they are rendered, then none carries a navigation entry or link to /specialties.html
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per owner decision)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page (owner decision; possible follow-up request)
filtering or searching by specialty (NG-9 scope; the page is a full listing)
a machine-readable form of the listing (cf. withdrawn REQ-VET-002)
notes: Scope quotes intake line 1 decisions. Narrowest-reading choices, recorded as open questions in docs/prd.md: an unheld specialty is listed and shown as held by none, matching REQ-VET-001's convention for a vet with none; order must be stable, with no rule stated; specialty names show as stored. REQ-SYS-001 still applies: the new page carries the shared navigation, and only inbound entries are excluded. No Non-Goals row changed, so scope_overrides is absent. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records. Surface: code; docs/prd.md was edited this dispatch for REQ-VET-003.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package as it stands (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts). Three small additions follow patterns already in force. (1) SpecialtyRepository: a narrow read-only Spring Data Repository<Specialty, Integer> returning every specialty. It mirrors PetTypeRepository's lookup-value precedent, and it is needed because Specialty has no back-reference and a specialty held by no veterinarian must still be listed. (2) SpecialtyDirectory: an immutable value object (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Value object) built from all specialties plus VetRepository.findAll(). It owns the inversion rule: each specialty with its holders, an unheld specialty kept with an empty list, a veterinarian with no specialty absent, and the stable order recorded on its Contracts row (specialties by name, veterinarians by last then first name, identity breaking ties). It holds strings and unmodifiable lists only, with no entity references, so it meets the closed Domain Core properties in full; the persistence-entity exception does not cover it. (3) VetController gains GET /specialties.html, which reads both repositories, hands them to SpecialtyDirectory, and selects vets/specialtyList. The grouping and ordering are domain decisions and must not live in the controller (architecture-principles § Web controller row; the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules). Basis for the covering symbols: grep and file reads of vet/VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, Specialty.java and owner/PetTypeRepository.java (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis). Design writes: Contracts rows (Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, VetController carry REQ-VET-003; new SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyRepository rows), one invariant sentence on the address-only reachability, and a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request input (no path variable, no query parameter, no form), so there is no binding target and no data binder setup. Any parameter added later would need its own binding entry.

Repository boundary, SpecialtyDirectory unit tests: no double. Build the directory from real Specialty and Vet instances (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, never mock internal code). The edge cases go here: unheld specialty, vet with no specialty, vet holding several, empty clinic, stable order.

Repository boundary, controller tests: hand-written doubles of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository registered as test beans. Both interfaces are narrow, so a hand-written double fits. A @MockitoBean stub is not sanctioned for the new tests (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, hand-write mocks).

Framework transport: MockMvc via @WebMvcTest(VetController.class), the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). Assert the view name, the model's directory, and the rendered names (first then last name, unheld specialty shown as held by none).

No-inbound-link criterion: assert over the template sources the way I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks templates. No template other than specialtyList.html may contain the /specialties.html route. The new page still includes the shared layout navigation (REQ-SYS-001).

Page wording: new message keys go into every bundle under src/main/resources/messages, including the held-by-none wording. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces REQ-LANG-002. Specialty names render as stored and are not looked up in bundles.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository precedent; SpecialtyRepository follows it but extends the narrower Repository rather than JpaRepository, because the page needs only a read
existing vet HTML handler shape: read from the repository, populate the model, return the view name
layout-fragment usage and the existing held-by-none rendering convention for a vet with no specialty (REQ-VET-001), which the unheld-specialty case mirrors

risks.risk: Specialty directory path (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-directory row) scales with specialties and veterinarians.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: two full reads and one in-memory grouping and sorting pass. Size is unrecorded, treated as bounded. No paging, by requirement.

risks.risk: Order instability: VetRepository.findAll() and an unordered specialty read carry no ORDER BY, and specialty names are not unique in any vendor schema.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory sorts explicitly, using the order on its Contracts row with identity as the final tie-break. Order never depends on database return order.

risks.risk: Lazy-load failure while rendering: open-in-view is disabled (system-design § Persistence).
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is eagerly fetched and SpecialtyDirectory holds only strings, so the template touches no managed entity.

risks.risk: Business rule leaking into VetController (architecture-principles § Web controller; § Design Validation Checklist).
risks.mitigation: The controller only fetches, delegates to SpecialtyDirectory and selects the view. The inversion, exclusion and ordering rules live in the value object and are unit-tested there.

risks.risk: Stale vet cache: VetRepository.findAll() is cached with no eviction (system-design § Open Questions 5).
risks.mitigation: Accepted as existing state, since the application has no write path for veterinarians or specialties (NG-2). SpecialtyRepository stays uncached, and no new cache is introduced.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Scoping: one behavior in one bounded context (vet); no re-split. Stable order choice fills the PRD open question 'Should the specialty directory order follow a stated rule?' as a design default. It is recorded on the SpecialtyDirectory Contracts row, and the owner may restate it. The design doc had no § Scale and Load section; this dispatch adds it with its first row. No ADR: the choices follow sanctioned in-force patterns and constrain no later slice (adr-template § When to Create an ADR). Security: read-only GET with no input and no new trust boundary. Output is escaped by Thymeleaf by default, so the template must use th:text, never th:utext, for stored specialty and veterinarian names (system-design § Threat Model, XSS row).

findings.description: The test cannot fail. Both specialties are named 'dentistry' and both vets are 'Sam Lee', and Listing carries only names. Any tie order therefore yields an equal SpecialtyDirectory, so removing the thenComparing(getId) tie-breakers in SpecialtyDirectory.java would leave it green. It asserts nothing about the identity tie-break that edge case 2 ('stable order') relies on. Ordering by name and by last then first name is already covered by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderSpecialtiesByNameAndVeterinariansByLastThenFirstName.
findings.fix: Delete this test. An identity tie between equal names is unobservable through the public output, so it needs no test. Alternatively, keep a stability test whose inputs differ visibly across the shuffled orders (distinct names fed in reversed order).

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Holder matching uses `vet.getSpecialties().contains(specialty)`, which relies on entity equality. A grep -F for 'boolean equals' and 'int hashCode' under src/main/java returns no match, so Specialty/NamedEntity/BaseEntity use identity equality. VetRepository.findAll is @Cacheable("vets") (VetRepository.java:45/55), so from the second request on the cached Vet instances carry Specialty objects loaded in an earlier session, while SpecialtyRepository.findAll() returns fresh instances. contains() is then false for every pair and every specialty renders as 'held by none'. This is reasoned from the code, not verified by running the app. SpecialtyDirectoryPageTests and SpecialtyDirectoryTests stub both repositories with shared instances, so no test reaches it. Match on identity of the stored row (Specialty::getId) rather than object identity.

The Scale and Load row for the specialty directory records time O(V*k + S log S + V log V). The code does not deliver that bound. Inside the per-specialty loop, each vet's `getSpecialties()` (Vet.java:60-64) re-sorts its whole specialty set on every call, and `contains` then scans the resulting List. The real cost is O(S*V*k log k). Computing each vet's specialty ids once, or grouping in a single pass over vets into a map keyed by specialty id, is equally clear and meets the recorded bound.
